title: 150 Years of Heidelberg Materials
content: # 150 Years of Heidelberg Materials. New Heidelberg Portland-Cement plant in Leimen, 1900. This account of the 150-year history of Heidelberg Materials traces the origins of the company. Developed in Great Britain, Portland cement also became a sought-after product in the German Confederation and later in the German Empire. In the middle of the Gründerzeit, in 1873, the trained beer brewer Johann Philipp Schifferdecker built a Portland cement plant in Heidelberg, which operated under the name "Portland-Cement-Werk Heidelberg, Schifferdecker & Söhne". As the city of Heidelberg prevented the rebuilding of the plant due to the dirt and noise pollution, the largest Portland cement plant in the German Empire was built in neighbouring Leimen. Otto was killed in the First World War, Ehrhart was plant manager in Leimen, a member of the board of directors and led the company after the Second World War. The company quickly developed into the leading group in southern Germany.

title: Heidelberg Materials - American Cement Association
content: # Heidelberg Materials. Heidelberg Materials is a leading supplier of cement, aggregates, ready mixed concrete, and asphalt in North America. With more than 450 locations, approximately 9,000 employees, a broad geographic footprint and a wide range of products, Heidelberg Materials is well positioned to support construction projects throughout the United States and Canada. Its history in the US traces back to 1897, as Lehigh Cement Company, which began as a single-mill operation in Ormrod, Pennsylvania. Over the years, it became one of North America’s leading providers of cement and construction materials, through a strategy of acquisitions, modernization, and increased productivity. Today, Heidelberg Materials serves cement customers in the US through 13 plants and a strong distribution network. The company manufactures and distributes gray cement, white cement, custom-colored cement, and slag cement. The majority of its cement is used in the production of ready-mixed concrete with the remainer used for precast concrete products, pipes, and blocks, and by the oil well industry.
